- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 10-15% above recent peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to reverse; add slight upward bias in next 3-5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (±0.3–0.5) and price is trending sideways; add 2-3% buffer to forecast.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative streak, model often misses the rebound; anticipate 1-2 day lag in upward correction.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; smooth sentiment over 3-5 days before adjusting forecast.
